title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Extended Protocol Errors Architecture
purpose: Define the DoQ adapter behavior for EDNS(0) tcp-keepalive rejection, server-initiated bidirectional stream detection, missing STREAM FIN timeout enforcement, and unknown/unexpected-context error code normalization.
design_summary: This slice adds four independent protocol-error enforcement mechanisms to the DoQ adapter. (1) The DoqMessageCodec gains an EDNS(0) tcp-keepalive option scanner that is invoked by DoqStream.ReadSingleMessageUntilFinAsync to reject messages containing the forbidden option with DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR. (2) The DoqClient starts a lightweight inbound stream monitor that treats any inbound (server-initiated) bidirectional stream as a fatal protocol error, closing the connection. (3) A configurable StreamFinTimeout property on DoqClient is applied to the read-until-FIN operation in QueryAsync; if the response payload arrives but STREAM FIN does not land within the timeout, the client closes the connection with DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR. (4) DoqErrorCode receives a static NormalizeReceivedErrorCode helper that maps undefined or unexpected-context application error codes to UnspecifiedError.
data_and_state_considerations: No new adapter state is required. The inbound stream monitor uses a fire-and-forget task pattern consistent with the existing server connection-handling model. The EDNS scanner is a pure function on byte slices. The FIN timeout is implemented via WaitAsync wrapping the ReadSingleMessageUntilFinAsync ValueTask.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The EDNS scanner must handle truncated DNS messages gracefully and return false for any non-tcp-keepalive EDNS option.
The FIN timeout must not interfere with the existing cancellation token path; both cancellation and timeout trigger DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR close.
The inbound stream monitor is started unconditionally for all DoqClient instances and gracefully shuts down on disposal.
Error code normalization handles any long value and maps both truly-unknown codes and unexpected-context codes to UnspecifiedError.
risks: The EDNS scanner is a simple byte-level parser and does not validate the overall DNS message structure beyond what is needed to locate EDNS options in the additional section.
The FIN timeout is a pure wall-clock WaitAsync; it does not distinguish between network latency and a truly missing FIN.
Server-initiated bidirectional stream detection is a defensive measure on the client; the server adapter remains unchanged and cannot open outbound streams by design.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: All four behaviors are implemented within the existing DoQ adapter files. No changes to the QUIC transport layer, codec architecture, or stream management patterns are required.

supplemental_sections.heading: EDNS tcp-keepalive Option Code
supplemental_sections.content: The EDNS(0) tcp-keepalive option code is 11 (0x000B). The scanner walks the DNS message additional section looking for an OPT pseudo-RR (type 41) and then scans its RDATA for the option code 0x000B.
